_README.purpose: Hand-curated rules that make matching work on REAL label text.
_README.why_not_in_data_processed: notebooks/run_analysis.py regenerates sensitivity_kb.json and ingredient_synonyms.json from its own hardcoded dicts. Anything hand-edited there is destroyed on the next run. This file is app-owned source and is never regenerated.
_README.STATUS: SEED DATA - NOT CLINICALLY REVIEWED. Entries below reflect well-established food-labelling facts, but this file governs allergen safety decisions and must be reviewed by a qualified dietitian or allergist before any real user relies on it.
_README.how_to_extend: hidden_forms: label terms that ARE a canonical allergen but share no obvious word with it. false_friends: phrases that LOOK like an allergen by word-match but are not. ambiguous: phrases that may or may not hide an allergen - always surfaced as CAUTION, never SAFE, never UNSAFE.

false_friends._comment: phrase -> canonical terms it must NOT be allowed to match. Prevents word-containment false positives that would erode trust.

ambiguous._comment: May or may not hide an allergen. Per product decision these are always surfaced as CAUTION with a reason - never silently cleared, never escalated to UNSAFE.

natural flavors.note: Manufacturers are not required to disclose the source of natural flavors; they can be dairy- or wheat-derived.

natural flavoring.note: Manufacturers are not required to disclose the source of natural flavoring.

artificial flavors.note: Carrier ingredients in flavor blends are not always disclosed.

flavoring.note: Unspecified flavoring may use a dairy or wheat carrier.

modified food starch.note: Usually corn in the US, but can be wheat-derived - especially on imported products.

dextrin.note: Dextrin can be produced from wheat starch.

caramel color.note: Can be produced from barley malt, though most commercial caramel color is corn-based.

hydrolyzed vegetable protein.note: Often wheat- or soy-derived, and a common source of free glutamates.

hydrolyzed protein.note: Source is frequently undisclosed; often wheat or soy.

yeast extract.note: May be grown on barley and contains naturally occurring glutamates.

spices.note: Spice blends can use wheat flour as an anti-caking agent.

seasoning.note: Seasoning blends commonly contain undisclosed wheat or dairy carriers.

broth.note: Commercial broths often contain wheat-based thickeners.

stock.note: Commercial stocks often contain wheat-based thickeners.

mono- and diglycerides.note: Can be animal-derived, including from dairy fat.

ambiguous._removed_lecithin: Deliberately NOT ambiguous. Lecithin is essentially always soy or sunflower, and even dairy-derived lecithin is a fat rather than a milk protein. Flagging it would fire on nearly every chocolate product and train users to dismiss warnings - which costs more safety than it buys.

flour.note: Unqualified 'flour' means wheat flour under US labelling convention.

surimi.note: Imitation crab is fish-based but commonly contains crab extract and wheat starch.
